choice.noRefField: This kind has no field that refers to other entries.
choice.noTarget: The field “{field}” does not point to a single kind with fields — choose in the scheme what it refers to.
choice.noText: This kind has no text field.
choice.noBack: No kind refers to this one (e.g. a translation to a word) — add such a field in the scheme.

asks.wordText: Field with the text of the word
asks.backField: Where the translations are (kind: field with the words)

thesis.label: Thesis: about what → thesis
thesis.says: On the front: what the statement is about (its reference fields, e.g. “Lk 1:35; Acts 1:8”), on the back its thesis — the first sentence. You grade yourself.
thesis.pattern: What does this statement say about: {0}?
thesis.name: Thesis

table.label: Table from the content: match the pairs
table.says: The rows of the first table in the content (column 1 ↔ column 2) to join into pairs; the thesis above them.
table.name: Table from the content

ask.label: Question about a field
ask.says: “Year of birth: Mickiewicz?” — type the value of the field.
ask.name: {field} (type it)

reverse.label: Reversed: who is it?
reverse.says: Shows the value of a field and asks for the entry (“Who was born in 1798?”).
reverse.name: Who: {field}

choose.label: Choice of four
choose.says: The correct value of the field and three values of this field from other entries.
choose.name: {field} (choice)

date.label: Date
date.says: When? — to the year, month or day.
date.name: {field} (date)

flash.label: Flashcard
flash.says: The first field on the front, the second on the back — you grade yourself.
flash.name: Flashcard: {front} → {back}

vocabulary.label: Word (each translation separately)
vocabulary.says: One card for each value of the second field — each translation.
vocabulary.name: Word: {front} → {back}

languages.label: Words: from language to language (both directions)
languages.says: The entry links words in several languages (e.g. a translation with a field “Words”): a separate card for each language — the words in that language with the direction (“English → Polish: house”), the answer is the words in the other languages.
languages.name: {field}: from language to language

whichLanguage.label: Words: which language is it?
whichLanguage.says: Shows a word and asks which language it is in — you tick every language in which a word with this spelling exists (e.g. “hotel”). Words with the same spelling make one card.
whichLanguage.pattern: Which language is “{0}”? Tick all in which it exists.
whichLanguage.name: Which language is it?

pairs.label: Words: match into pairs
pairs.says: Several translations at once: words in one language on the left, in the other on the right — you match them into pairs. Takes this translation and others at random; the languages are those of this translation.
pairs.name: Match into pairs

chooseTranslations.label: Words: tick the translations
chooseTranslations.says: Shows a word; you tick all its translations — in one or several languages — among them and a few other words of those languages.
chooseTranslations.name: Tick the translations

translateWord.label: Words: translate the word (each language separately)
translateWord.says: Shows a word and asks for its translation — a separate card for each language it has translations in; all translations into that language are correct.
translateWord.name: Translate the word

gaps.label: Gaps in a quote
gaps.says: Splits the text into pieces and asks for each — the pieces first, then the whole.
gaps.name: Gaps: {field}

temporal.label: By what I know
temporal.says: First what is due (weakest first), then new and forgotten — from the basics to the details; when nothing is left, in advance what you know least well; stacks of 20.
temporal.name: Daily review

once.label: Everything once
once.says: The whole set, each card once — a test.
once.name: Everything once

levels.label: Levels
levels.says: A good answer raises the card a level, a wrong one sends it back to the first; it ends when everything is at the top.
levels.name: Levels

due.label: Only overdue
due.says: Only cards that are due, by knowledge.
due.name: Overdue

gated.label: Basics first
gated.says: A card comes in only once what it requires (“Must be known first”) is mastered; missing basics come in by themselves. Built from ordinary steps: “Follow the learning order”, “Knowledge filter”, order “general first”.
gated.name: From the basics

general.label: From the general to the detail
general.says: The most general first; an entry that lies under another in the structure (a year under a stage, a stage under the whole life) comes in once that one is known. Built from the “Knowledge filter” and the order “general first”.
general.name: From the general to the detail

story.label: Story about a person (template)
story.says: A reminder, the person’s entry from the slot {osoba}, a question, the end — to use with different people.
story.name: Story about a person

chapters.label: Course with chapters
chapters.says: Choosing a chapter, each with content and a question; it ends when all are done.
chapters.name: Course

dialogue.label: Conversation with a character
dialogue.says: A character speaks, the learner chooses an answer; the choice changes closeness.
dialogue.question: What will you answer?
dialogue.name: Conversation
